scenario.title: Elements: A River Worth Returning To
scenario.premise: Starting from four storybook elements, travel from an orchard to a coastal gathering. Make useful things for people you meet. The world remembers what you leave behind.

stage.title: Four beginnings
stage.speaker: The keeper
stage.motivation: The river gathering is a month away. We begin with earth, water, air and fire. Make a bowl for supper and bricks for a hearth.
stage.travelText: Our next stop: Four beginnings. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

things.label: Earth
things.description: Loose ground: mineral grit, clay and the material in which roots grow.

things.label: Water
things.description: Flowing, soaking and carrying; a liquid that takes the shape of its container.

things.label: Air
things.description: The invisible moving world around us. It carries moisture and feeds a flame.

things.label: Fire
things.description: Heat and light. It cooks, hardens and changes materials rather than merely joining them.

scenario.title: Elements: A River Worth Returning To

stage.title: What the water hides
stage.speaker: The naturalist
stage.motivation: There is a whole country in a drop of pond water. Make a microscope and a clear slide so we can show it at the gathering.
stage.travelText: Our next stop: What the water hides. Bring the useful things; leave the rest where we made them.

areas.label: A light to come home to

things.label: Bowl
things.description: An open, hollow vessel with a broad mouth and a stable base.

things.label: Wood
things.description: Rough timber: solid lengths with grain and bulk, not flat boards yet.

things.label: Sand
things.description: Small, hard mineral grains. Loose when poured, abrasive when rubbed.

things.label: Glass
things.description: A hard, clear material that lets light through but needs shaping to give it a particular job.

things.label: Planks
things.description: Flat, cut boards with broad faces and straight edges; easier to join into surfaces than rough timber.

things.label: Hollow tube
things.description: A small wooden tube with an open interior, ready to carry air or hold aligned parts.

locations.label: Mill pond
locations.description: Still pond water, collected for observation.

args: Voluntary stop after completing Food for the crossing (stage 21), before Water for everyone. This was fresh logical-interface play from an authored stage-18 checkpoint, not a full-campaign or human-player claim. I continued because I wanted to discover the pond life, then enjoyed making a flora and provisions for the gathering. Sand plus glass making a lens, collecting pond water with the bowl, observing a leaf through the lens, cider changing to vinegar, and netting fish from the shore were satisfying. Botany was my favourite complete sequence: observe, draw, then join the drawing with the preserved specimen collection. The food chapter was straightforward and pleasantly so, not a difficulty problem. Weather was more routine, and I expected windsock plus paper to make a wind record by analogy with rain-gauge plus paper; it did not. I used two hints in optics, for glass and lens. Glass plus planks making a glass slide remained obscure to me. I also tried plant plus bound-book before learning the plant first needed paper, which felt a fussy distinction. My biggest disappointment was making both Microscope and Pond slide, then getting No new combination here when I put the slide on the microscope. The invitation promised a country in a drop, but I never got an observation payoff there. Making the objects completed the request instead. By the end I wanted the actual gathering, not another preparation list; the next Water for everyone invitation did not pull me onward now. No tool or permission blocker. No visits, undo, or hidden-file inspection; earlier earned equipment and history were supplied by the checkpoint.
